verdicts.human_summary: logger.error already applies error color internally, so passing CLI_COLORS.error(...) results in redundant/nested ANSI codes. Suggests using plain string instead.
verdicts.reasoning: AI Comment 1 identifies the exact same issue at the same line: double application of color when CLI_COLORS.error() is passed to logger.error(). Both comments point out the redundant ANSI wrapping. The AI comment even references the same specific call `logger.error(CLI_COLORS.error('Smoke tests failed.'))`. While the AI comment hedges more ('in practice this is harmless') and suggests adding a clarifying comment rather than removing the wrapping, the core concern about redundant double-coloring is the same.
